policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'on the right side' renders either the qere mi-yamin ('from/at the right') or the ketiv be-yamin ('on the right'); the English preposition 'on' does not distinguish min from bet here, and there is no mapped textual note.

ASV 'into the hands of them that did the work' is plural 'hands', matching the qere plural construct yede; the ketiv singular yad would read 'into the hand of'. The hebrew_gloss note ('brought it forth') is about a different word and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 'that had the oversight of the house' renders either the qere hophal participle ('those appointed over') or the unpointed ketiv hpqdym (qal 'overseers' or passive 'appointed ones'); the English does not distinguish active from passive here, and the only note (hebrew_gloss) concerns other wording.
